Consider the photochemical monobromination of the following alkylcyclohexanes:
(I) Methylcyclohexane
(II) Ethylcyclohexane
(III) Isopropylcyclohexane
(IV) sec-Butylcyclohexane

In which of these compounds will the major monobrominated product have the bromine atom attached directly to a carbon atom of the cyclohexane ring?
questions.question:
Consider the photochemical monobromination of the following alkylcyclohexanes:
(I) Methylcyclohexane
(II) Ethylcyclohexane
(III) Isopropylcyclohexane
(IV) sec-Butylcyclohexane

In which of these compounds will the major monobrominated product have the bromine atom attached directly to a carbon atom of the cyclohexane ring?
questions.solution:
Photochemical bromination is highly regioselective, favoring the formation of the most stable free radical intermediate. We must compare the stability of the tertiary radical on the cyclohexane ring versus the most stable radical on the alkyl side chain for each compound by counting hyperconjugative $\alpha$-hydrogens.

(I) Methylcyclohexane:
- Ring tertiary radical: 4 $\alpha$-H (from ring) + 3 $\alpha$-H (from methyl) = 7 $\alpha$-H.
- Side chain radical (primary): 1 $\alpha$-H (from ring).
The ring radical is much more stable, so bromination occurs on the ring.

(II) Ethylcyclohexane:
- Ring tertiary radical: 4 $\alpha$-H (from ring) + 2 $\alpha$-H (from ethyl $\text{CH}_2$) = 6 $\alpha$-H.
- Side chain secondary radical (on $\text{CH}_2$): 1 $\alpha$-H (from ring) + 3 $\alpha$-H (from methyl) = 4 $\alpha$-H.
The ring radical has more $\alpha$-H ($6 > 4$), so bromination occurs on the ring.

(III) Isopropylcyclohexane:
- Ring tertiary radical: 4 $\alpha$-H (from ring) + 1 $\alpha$-H (from isopropyl $\text{CH}$) = 5 $\alpha$-H.
- Side chain tertiary radical: 1 $\alpha$-H (from ring) + 6 $\alpha$-H (from two methyls) = 7 $\alpha$-H.
The side chain radical is more stable ($7 > 5$), so bromination occurs on the side chain.

(IV) sec-Butylcyclohexane:
- Ring tertiary radical: 4 $\alpha$-H (from ring) + 1 $\alpha$-H (from sec-butyl $\text{CH}$) = 5 $\alpha$-H.
- Side chain tertiary radical: 1 $\alpha$-H (from ring) + 3 $\alpha$-H (from methyl) + 2 $\alpha$-H (from $\text{CH}_2$) = 6 $\alpha$-H.
The side chain radical is more stable ($6 > 5$), so bromination occurs on the side chain.

Therefore, only compounds (I) and (II) yield a major product with the bromine atom on the cyclohexane ring.

Answer: I and II only

Condition I: Treatment with a large excess of $\text{NaSH}$ in acetone.
Condition II: Heating in pure methanol.

Which of the following correctly describes the predominant mechanism and the stereochemical outcome for Condition I and Condition II, respectively?
questions.question:
(S)-2-Bromopentane is subjected to two different reaction conditions:
Condition I: Treatment with a large excess of $\text{NaSH}$ in acetone.
Condition II: Heating in pure methanol.

Which of the following correctly describes the predominant mechanism and the stereochemical outcome for Condition I and Condition II, respectively?
options: Condition I: $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$, Racemization; Condition II: $\text{S}_{\text{N}}2$, Inversion
Condition I: $\text{S}_{\text{N}}2$, Inversion; Condition II: $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$, Racemization
Condition I: $\text{S}_{\text{N}}2$, Retention; Condition II: $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$, Racemization
Condition I: $\text{S}_{\text{N}}2$, Inversion; Condition II: $\text{S}_{\text{N}}2$, Inversion
questions.solution:
For Condition I: The substrate is a secondary alkyl halide. $\text{NaSH}$ provides a strong nucleophile ($\text{SH}^{-}$) and acetone is a polar aprotic solvent. A high concentration of a strong nucleophile in a polar aprotic solvent strongly favours the $\text{S}_{\text{N}}2$ mechanism. The $\text{S}_{\text{N}}2$ reaction proceeds with complete inversion of configuration.

For Condition II: Heating the secondary alkyl halide in pure methanol (a polar protic solvent) without any added strong nucleophile corresponds to solvolysis. Under these conditions, the weak nucleophile and ionizing solvent favour the formation of a carbocation intermediate, leading to the $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$ mechanism. The $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$ reaction results in racemization of the chiral centre.

Therefore, Condition I follows $\text{S}_{\text{N}}2$ with inversion, and Condition II follows $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$ with racemization.

Answer: Condition I: $\text{S}_{\text{N}}2$, Inversion; Condition II: $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$, Racemization

When these optically active isomers are separately treated with sodium ethoxide in ethanol, the number of isomers that yield an alkene as the major product is ____.
questions.question: Among all the structural isomers of $\mathrm{C}_{5}\mathrm{H}_{11}\mathrm{Br}$, first identify those which are optically active. When these optically active isomers are separately treated with sodium ethoxide in ethanol, the number of isomers that yield an alkene as the major product is ____.
questions.solution:
First, we identify the optically active structural isomers of $\mathrm{C}_{5}\mathrm{H}_{11}\mathrm{Br}$. A molecule is optically active if it contains a chiral center (a carbon atom bonded to four different groups).
The 8 structural isomers of $\mathrm{C}_{5}\mathrm{H}_{11}\mathrm{Br}$ are:
1. 1-bromopentane (achiral)
2. 2-bromopentane (chiral at C2, $2^{\circ}$ halide)
3. 3-bromopentane (achiral)
4. 1-bromo-3-methylbutane (achiral)
5. 2-bromo-3-methylbutane (chiral at C2, $2^{\circ}$ halide)
6. 1-bromo-2-methylbutane (chiral at C2, $1^{\circ}$ halide)
7. 2-bromo-2-methylbutane (achiral)
8. 1-bromo-2,2-dimethylpropane (achiral)

There are 3 optically active isomers: 2-bromopentane, 2-bromo-3-methylbutane, and 1-bromo-2-methylbutane.

Next, we consider their reaction with sodium ethoxide ($\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{H}_{5}\mathrm{ONa}$) in ethanol. Ethoxide is a strong base and a strong nucleophile.
- For $1^{\circ}$ alkyl halides, substitution ($\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}}2$) is favored over elimination, yielding an ether as the major product. Thus, 1-bromo-2-methylbutane yields an ether as the major product.
- For $2^{\circ}$ alkyl halides, elimination ($\mathrm{E}2$) is favored over substitution, yielding an alkene as the major product. Thus, 2-bromopentane and 2-bromo-3-methylbutane yield alkenes as their major products.

Therefore, exactly 2 of the optically active isomers yield an alkene as the major product.

Answer: $2$

questions.q: What is the major organic product formed when 1-bromo-4-chlorobutane is reacted with exactly 1 equivalent of KNO$_2$?
questions.question: What is the major organic product formed when 1-bromo-4-chlorobutane is reacted with exactly 1 equivalent of KNO$_2$?
questions.solution:
The substrate, 1-bromo-4-chlorobutane, contains two primary halogens: bromine and chlorine.

Bromide is a better leaving group than chloride because the C-Br bond is weaker than the C-Cl bond. When exactly 1 equivalent of a nucleophile is used, substitution will occur preferentially at the carbon bearing the bromine atom.

The reagent KNO$_2$ is an ionic compound and provides the nitrite ion (NO$_2^-$) in solution. The nitrite ion is an ambidentate nucleophile. Attack occurs predominantly through the more electron-rich oxygen atom, leading to the formation of an alkyl nitrite (-O-N=O). In contrast, AgNO$_2$ would lead to a nitroalkane (-NO$_2$).

Therefore, the bromine atom is replaced by a nitrite group, yielding 4-chlorobutyl nitrite as the major organic product.

Answer: 4-chlorobutyl nitrite

questions.q: When 3-bromo-3-methylpentane is heated with sodium methoxide in methanol, an elimination reaction occurs. What is the IUPAC name of the major organic product formed?
questions.question: When 3-bromo-3-methylpentane is heated with sodium methoxide in methanol, an elimination reaction occurs. What is the IUPAC name of the major organic product formed?
questions.solution:
The reaction of a tertiary alkyl halide (3-bromo-3-methylpentane) with a strong, unhindered base (sodium methoxide) under heating conditions proceeds via an E2 elimination mechanism.

According to Saytzeff's rule, the major product is the more highly substituted alkene. The substrate has two types of $\beta$-hydrogens: those on the adjacent methylene carbons (C2 and C4) and those on the methyl group attached to C3.

Elimination of a hydrogen from the methylene group yields 3-methylpent-2-ene, which is a trisubstituted alkene.

Elimination of a hydrogen from the methyl group yields 2-ethylbut-1-ene, which is a disubstituted alkene.

Therefore, the more stable trisubstituted alkene, 3-methylpent-2-ene, is formed as the major product.

Answer: 3-methylpent-2-ene

questions.question: An optically active alkyl halide undergoes a nucleophilic substitution reaction. The resulting product mixture is found to be completely optically inactive. The reaction follows first-order kinetics and proceeds via a pentacoordinate transition state.
The reaction follows first-order kinetics and proceeds via a planar carbocation intermediate.
The reaction follows second-order kinetics and proceeds via a planar carbocation intermediate.
questions.solution:

The $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$ mechanism is a two-step process that follows first-order kinetics, where the rate-determining step is the formation of a planar carbocation intermediate.

The nucleophile can then attack this planar carbocation from either face with roughly equal probability, leading to a racemic mixture.

Answer: The reaction follows first-order kinetics and proceeds via a planar carbocation intermediate.

Further chlorination of 2-chloropentane can take place at any of the five carbon atoms, yielding the following structurally distinct dichloro compounds:

1. Chlorination at C-1: $CH_2Cl-CHCl-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3$ (1,2-dichloropentane)

2. Chlorination at C-2: $CH_3-CCl_2-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3$ (2,2-dichloropentane)

3. Chlorination at C-3: $CH_3-CHCl-CHCl-CH_2-CH_3$ (2,3-dichloropentane)

4. Chlorination at C-4: $CH_3-CHCl-CH_2-CHCl-CH_3$ (2,4-dichloropentane)

5. Chlorination at C-5: $CH_3-CHCl-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2Cl$ (1,4-dichloropentane)

Since all five positions yield different structural isomers, a total of 5 structurally distinct dichloro compounds are obtained.

Answer: $5$

Aniline is treated with $\text{NaNO}_2$ and $\text{HCl}$ at $0\text{-}5^\circ\text{C}$ to form intermediate A. Intermediate A is then treated with $\text{Cu}_2\text{Cl}_2/\text{HCl}$ to form compound B. Finally, compound B is reacted with sodium in dry ether to yield compound C.

Identify the name of the reaction forming B from A, the name of the reaction forming C from B, and the identity of compound C, respectively.
questions.question:
Aniline is treated with $\text{NaNO}_2$ and $\text{HCl}$ at $0\text{-}5^\circ\text{C}$ to form intermediate A. Intermediate A is then treated with $\text{Cu}_2\text{Cl}_2/\text{HCl}$ to form compound B. Finally, compound B is reacted with sodium in dry ether to yield compound C.

Identify the name of the reaction forming B from A, the name of the reaction forming C from B, and the identity of compound C, respectively.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Aniline reacts with $\text{NaNO}_2/\text{HCl}$ at $0\text{-}5^\circ\text{C}$ to undergo diazotization, forming benzenediazonium chloride (Intermediate A).

Step 2: Benzenediazonium chloride (A) reacts with $\text{Cu}_2\text{Cl}_2/\text{HCl}$ to form chlorobenzene (Compound B). The use of cuprous chloride ($\text{Cu}_2\text{Cl}_2$) to replace the diazonium group with a chlorine atom is known as the Sandmeyer reaction.

Step 3: Chlorobenzene (B) reacts with sodium ($\text{Na}$) in dry ether. This is a coupling reaction of two aryl halides, known as the Fittig reaction, which yields biphenyl (Compound C).

Therefore, the sequence involves the Sandmeyer reaction followed by the Fittig reaction, and the final product is biphenyl.

Answer: Sandmeyer reaction, Fittig reaction, Biphenyl

questions.question: Monochlorination of n-butane under photochemical conditions produces a compound 'P' which possesses a chiral center. The racemic mixture of 'P' is isolated and subjected to further chlorination to yield a mixture of dichloro products. The total number of stereoisomers of the dichloro products formed and the number of fractions obtained upon fractional distillation of this mixture are respectively:
questions.solution:
The structure of n-butane is $CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3$. Monochlorination yields 1-chlorobutane and 2-chlorobutane. Only 2-chlorobutane has a chiral center, so 'P' is 2-chlorobutane.

Further chlorination of racemic 2-chlorobutane yields four structural isomers. Let us analyze the stereoisomers and fractions for each:

1. 1,2-dichlorobutane ($CH_2Cl-C^{*}HCl-CH_2-CH_3$): Has one chiral center. Forms a racemic pair (d and l). This contributes 2 stereoisomers and 1 fraction.

2. 2,2-dichlorobutane ($CH_3-CCl_2-CH_2-CH_3$): Achiral. Contributes 1 stereoisomer and 1 fraction.

3. 2,3-dichlorobutane ($CH_3-C^{*}HCl-C^{*}HCl-CH_3$): Has two similar chiral centers. It exists as a meso compound and a racemic pair (d and l). This contributes 3 stereoisomers. The meso form and the racemic pair have different boiling points, yielding 2 fractions.

4. 1,3-dichlorobutane ($CH_3-C^{*}HCl-CH_2-CH_2Cl$): Has one chiral center. Forms a racemic pair (d and l). This contributes 2 stereoisomers and 1 fraction.

Total number of stereoisomers = $2 + 1 + 3 + 2 = 8$.

Total number of fractions = $1 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 5$.

Answer: $8, 5$

The rate of an $\text{S}_{\text{N}}2$ reaction is maximised in a polar aprotic solvent (like acetone), which solvates cations (like $\text{Na}^+$) but leaves the nucleophilic anions unsolvated and highly reactive.

4) Chlorination of the C3-methyl group gives 3-(chloromethyl)pentane. It is also achiral due to two equivalent ethyl groups, forming 1 fraction.

Total number of fractions = 1 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 5.

Answer: $5$

questions.question: Which of the following reagents is most appropriate to selectively convert 2-bromo-2,3-dimethylbutane into 2,3-dimethylbut-1-ene as the major product?
questions.solution:
The substrate, 2-bromo-2,3-dimethylbutane, is a tertiary alkyl halide. Elimination can occur at two different $\beta$-positions to give either 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene (the more substituted Saytzeff product) or 2,3-dimethylbut-1-ene (the less substituted Hofmann product).

The desired major product is 2,3-dimethylbut-1-ene, which is the Hofmann product. To reverse the normal regioselectivity and favor the formation of the less substituted alkene, a sterically bulky strong base must be used.

Potassium tert-butoxide is a bulky base that selectively abstracts the more accessible primary $\beta$-hydrogen due to steric hindrance, leading to the Hofmann product.

Sodium ethoxide is a small base and would predominantly yield the Saytzeff product. Aqueous KOH favors nucleophilic substitution to form an alcohol, and ethanolic AgCN leads to isocyanide formation.

Answer: Potassium tert-butoxide in tert-butyl alcohol

Which of the following nucleophiles corresponds to the reaction pathway with the activation energy $E_{a1}$?

questions.solution:
The activation energy of an $\mathrm{S_{N}2}$ reaction is inversely related to the reactivity of the nucleophile. The reaction with the lowest activation energy ($E_{a1}$) corresponds to the fastest reaction, which requires the strongest nucleophile.

$\mathrm{CH_{3}COO^{-}}$ versus $\mathrm{H_{2}O}$: Anionic nucleophiles are generally stronger than neutral species, making acetate stronger than water.

The overall order of nucleophilicity is $\mathrm{SH^{-}} > \mathrm{OH^{-}} > \mathrm{CH_{3}COO^{-}} > \mathrm{H_{2}O}$.

Therefore, the strongest nucleophile, $\mathrm{SH^{-}}$, corresponds to the lowest activation energy barrier, $E_{a1}$.

Hexamethylbenzene contains a benzene ring, which has a delocalized system of 6 $\pi$ electrons.

The total number of $\pi$ electrons in one molecule of C and one molecule of D is $4 + 6 = 10$.

questions.question: When isopropylcyclopentane is reacted with $\text{Br}_2$ in the presence of sunlight, a major monobrominated product $P$ is formed. Compound $P$ is then heated with alcoholic $\text{KOH}$ to give a major alkene $Q$. Identify the structure of $Q$.
questions.solution:
First, we determine the major product $P$ of the photochemical bromination of isopropylcyclopentane. Bromination is highly regioselective and occurs at the position that yields the most stable free radical.

Isopropylcyclopentane has two distinct tertiary carbons: one on the cyclopentane ring and one on the isopropyl group.
- The radical formed at the ring tertiary carbon is stabilized by 5 $\alpha$-hydrogens (4 from the two adjacent ring $\text{CH}_2$ groups and 1 from the isopropyl $\text{CH}$ group).
- The radical formed at the isopropyl tertiary carbon is stabilized by 7 $\alpha$-hydrogens (1 from the adjacent ring $\text{CH}$ group and 6 from the two methyl groups).

Since $7 > 5$, the tertiary radical on the isopropyl group is more stable. Thus, bromination occurs predominantly on the side chain, making $P$ (2-bromopropan-2-yl)cyclopentane.

Next, compound $P$ undergoes dehydrohalogenation (E2 elimination) upon heating with alcoholic $\text{KOH}$. The elimination can occur in two directions:
- Removal of a $\beta$-hydrogen from one of the methyl groups yields a disubstituted alkene, (prop-1-en-2-yl)cyclopentane.
- Removal of the $\beta$-hydrogen from the cyclopentane ring yields a tetrasubstituted alkene, isopropylidenecyclopentane.

According to Saytzeff's rule, the more highly substituted alkene is the major product. Therefore, the major product $Q$ is isopropylidenecyclopentane.

Answer: Isopropylidenecyclopentane

If the solvent is changed to methanol (a polar protic solvent), the $\text{I}^-$ ions will be heavily solvated through hydrogen bonding. This solvation lowers the ground state energy of the nucleophile, thereby increasing the activation energy required to reach the transition state. As a result, the reaction rate decreases significantly in methanol compared to acetone.

Answer: Major product is (2S)-2-iodopentane; the reaction rate decreases in methanol.

Dichlorination of cyclopentane produces three structural isomers: 1,1-dichlorocyclopentane, 1,2-dichlorocyclopentane, and 1,3-dichlorocyclopentane.

1. 1,1-dichlorocyclopentane has no chiral centers and does not show stereoisomerism. (1 isomer)

2. 1,2-dichlorocyclopentane has two chiral centers. The cis-isomer has a plane of symmetry and is a meso compound (1 isomer). The trans-isomer lacks a plane of symmetry and exists as a pair of enantiomers (2 isomers). Total = 3 isomers.

3. 1,3-dichlorocyclopentane also has two chiral centers. Similar to the 1,2-isomer, the cis-form is a meso compound (1 isomer), while the trans-form is chiral and exists as a pair of enantiomers (2 isomers). Total = 3 isomers.

Total number of dichlorinated isomers = $1 + 3 + 3 = 7$.

Answer: $7$

questions.q:
Consider the following reaction sequence:
$\text{Aniline} \xrightarrow{\text{NaNO}_2 + \text{HCl}, \, 273-278 \text{ K}} (\text{A})$
$(\text{A}) \xrightarrow{\text{Cu powder} / \text{HCl}} (\text{B})$
$(\text{B}) \xrightarrow{\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}, \, \text{Na} / \text{dry ether}} (\text{C})$

Identify the correct names for the reactions involved in the conversions $(\text{A}) \rightarrow (\text{B})$ and $(\text{B}) \rightarrow (\text{C})$, respectively.
questions.question:
Consider the following reaction sequence:
$\text{Aniline} \xrightarrow{\text{NaNO}_2 + \text{HCl}, \, 273-278 \text{ K}} (\text{A})$
$(\text{A}) \xrightarrow{\text{Cu powder} / \text{HCl}} (\text{B})$
$(\text{B}) \xrightarrow{\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}, \, \text{Na} / \text{dry ether}} (\text{C})$

Identify the correct names for the reactions involved in the conversions $(\text{A}) \rightarrow (\text{B})$ and $(\text{B}) \rightarrow (\text{C})$, respectively.
questions.solution:
The first step is the diazotisation of aniline using $\text{NaNO}_2$ and $\text{HCl}$ at $273-278 \text{ K}$, which yields benzene diazonium chloride as product (A).

In the next step, benzene diazonium chloride (A) reacts with copper powder and $\text{HCl}$ to form chlorobenzene as product (B). The use of copper powder (instead of cuprous chloride) specifically characterizes this as the Gatterman reaction.

Finally, chlorobenzene (B) reacts with methyl chloride ($\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$) and sodium in the presence of dry ether to form toluene (C). The coupling of an aryl halide with an alkyl halide using sodium metal is known as the Wurtz-Fittig reaction.

Thus, the sequence of named reactions is Gatterman reaction followed by Wurtz-Fittig reaction.

Answer: Gatterman reaction and Wurtz-Fittig reaction

questions.question: The total number of isomeric products (including stereoisomers) obtained on monochlorination of 2,2,4-trimethylpentane is
questions.solution:
Structure of 2,2,4-trimethylpentane is $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_3$.

There are four distinct types of hydrogen atoms in this molecule, leading to four structural isomers upon monochlorination:

1. Substitution at one of the $t$-butyl methyl groups yields 1-chloro-2,2,4-trimethylpentane. This molecule has no chiral center. (1 isomer)

2. Substitution at the $\text{CH}_2$ group yields 3-chloro-2,2,4-trimethylpentane. The C-3 carbon becomes a chiral center as it is attached to four different groups: $-\text{H}$, $-\text{Cl}$, $-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_3$, and $-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$. (2 stereoisomers)

3. Substitution at the $\text{CH}$ group yields 2-chloro-2,4,4-trimethylpentane. This molecule has no chiral center. (1 isomer)

4. Substitution at one of the isopropyl methyl groups yields 1-chloro-2,4,4-trimethylpentane. The C-2 carbon becomes a chiral center as it is attached to four different groups: $-\text{H}$, $-\text{CH}_3$, $-\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$, and $-\text{CH}_2\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_3$. (2 stereoisomers)

Total number of isomers = $1 + 2 + 1 + 2 = 6$.

Answer: $6$

questions.q: Consider the dehydrohalogenation of cis-1-bromo-2-methylcyclohexane and trans-1-bromo-2-methylcyclohexane using alcoholic KOH. Identify the major alkene product formed in each case.
questions.question: Consider the dehydrohalogenation of cis-1-bromo-2-methylcyclohexane and trans-1-bromo-2-methylcyclohexane using alcoholic KOH. Identify the major alkene product formed in each case.
options: Both isomers yield 1-methylcyclohexene as the major product.
The cis-isomer yields 3-methylcyclohexene and the trans-isomer yields 1-methylcyclohexene.
Both isomers yield 3-methylcyclohexene as the major product.
The cis-isomer yields 1-methylcyclohexene and the trans-isomer yields 3-methylcyclohexene.
questions.solution:
Dehydrohalogenation via the E2 mechanism requires an anti-periplanar arrangement of the leaving group (Br) and the beta-hydrogen. In a cyclohexane ring, this means both the Br atom and the beta-hydrogen must occupy axial positions.

For cis-1-bromo-2-methylcyclohexane:
In the chair conformation where Br is axial, the methyl group at C2 is equatorial. This leaves the hydrogen at C2 in an axial position. There are also axial hydrogens at C6. Elimination can occur at either C2 or C6. Following Zaitsev's rule, the more substituted alkene is preferred, making 1-methylcyclohexene the major product.

For trans-1-bromo-2-methylcyclohexane:
In the reactive chair conformation where Br is axial, the methyl group at C2 must also be axial (since they are trans). Consequently, there is no axial hydrogen at C2. The only available beta-axial hydrogens are at C6. Therefore, elimination can only occur between C1 and C6, yielding 3-methylcyclohexene as the sole (and thus major) product.

Thus, the cis-isomer yields 1-methylcyclohexene, and the trans-isomer yields 3-methylcyclohexene.

Answer: The cis-isomer yields 1-methylcyclohexene and the trans-isomer yields 3-methylcyclohexene.
